terms.grammar: adjective, interrogative and relative, third declension
evidence: Mart. 12.92.4: sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?
Traupman 406: what kind of, what sort of, quālis
terms.comment: As a relative it answers tālis: tālis … quālis, such … as. In an exclamation, “what … !”: quālis erat!, how he looked! (Verg. A. 2.274). The noun is also used: quod genus …? (see “kind”).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 15.20.3: cupiō cognōscere iter tuum cujus modī sit (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: what sort of man is he?
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.134: quid hominis sit, what sort of a man he is (Lewis & Short s.v. quis)
terms.comment: Literally “what of a man”: said of a person’s character, often in surprise. So Quid negōtī est?, what’s the matter?

phrases.latin: dīc mihi, sī fīās tū leō, quālis eris?
phrases.english: tell me, if you turned into a lion, what kind of lion would you be?

phrases.latin: ei mihi, quālis erat, quantum mūtātus ab illō
phrases.english: ah me, what he looked like! how changed from the man he was

phrases.latin: lupus est homō hominī, nōn homō, quom quālis sit nōn nōvit.
phrases.english: man is a wolf to man, not a man, when he doesn’t know what sort of man the other is.

phrases.latin: gallīna erat lignea patentibus in orbem ālīs, quālēs esse solent quae incubant ōva
phrases.english: there was a wooden hen with its wings spread round, as hens have them when they sit on eggs
